entries.hypothesis: With 256 equal scores, signed 8-bit probabilities round every element to zero.
entries.outcome: Reproduced the 2026-11-11 pilot exactly. 256 tokens: P8 signed code 0 (zero row), P9 signed 1, P10 signed 2, P8 unsigned (qmax 255) 1. At 1024 tokens all are zero.
entries.limitations: Synthetic; says nothing about real data.

entries.hypothesis: The INT8 loss comes from attention-probability precision (flat rows), not from weights or linear activations.
entries.outcome: 10 variants on the canonical validation split (47,580 windows / 195 files; paired file bootstrap). Flat-row hypothesis REJECTED by the frozen gate: 0 all-zero attention rows in P8-signed (the hypothesis target) and in every other variant except uniform INT8 (zero-row rate 3.7e-6; 170 of 47,580 windows contain at least one all-zero row; corrected 2026-11-14 after the audit) (criteria 1 and 2 fail). Mechanism found instead: probability-mass truncation (row mass 0.986 INT10 / 0.829 P8-signed / 0.948 P8-unsigned; nonzero entries per row 185 / 79 / 137; context error 0.074 / 0.225 / 0.115). Macro-F1 change vs INT10 (pp): W8 -0.01 [-0.12,0.14]; A8 -0.62; P8 signed -1.27; P8 unsigned +0.49 [-0.18,1.21]; uniform INT8 -1.82; W8A8+P10 -0.65; W8A8+P8u -0.23 [-1.36,0.38]. P9-signed and P8-unsigned are the same quantizer (qmax 255) and give identical outputs (consistency check). Accuracy gate passed by: W8, P8u(=P9s), W8A8+P8u(=P9s).
entries.limitations: Float-input path (input quantized at the variant's own input scale); a W8A8 hardware variant would also need an 8-bit on-chip preprocessing constant. Validation only; per-class CIs are wide (normal class has 5 validation files).
entries.next_action: Precision finalists for A05: W8A8+P8u (largest expected saving) and/or P8u alone; requires a versioned export, HLS types, own goldens and an integrated build to test the >= 15 % post-route gate.

entries.hypothesis: Some HLS widths exceed proven legal ranges; narrowing them is exact and cheaper.
entries.status: implemented (proof + exhaustive check for the softmax divider)
entries.outcome: Survey of the canonical HLS report: HLS already narrows most requant multipliers (23-24 bit x 32 bit). Candidate not inferred by HLS: attention context requant (df_head_*: mul_33s_33ns_64). Proof sketch: row sum of probability codes <= 511 + 256/2 = 639, |v| <= 511 -> |context accumulator| <= 326,529 < 2^19 (20-bit signed). Second candidate found and taken to A04: the softmax divider (quotient <= 511).
entries.next_action: single-operator HLS + Vivado OOC probe (A04) of the context requant: original vs proven-width

entries.hypothesis: Silent class corruption is concentrated in a few stage groups.
entries.command: python -m tools.research.fault_injection campaign --out artifacts/research/B01_20261113; python -m tools.research.fault_injection weights|vote --out artifacts/research/B01_20261113
entries.outcome: 3,072 transient single-bit flips (8 groups x 3 bit bands x 128) on 256 validation windows (64/class); injection disabled = canonical logits on all 256. Silent class corruptions 75: G8 logits high bits 42, G1 input codes high bits 28, G2 projection accumulator mid bits 4, G3 QKV high 1. Attention scores/probabilities/context: 0 class changes in 3 x 384 injections. Proven-range check C2 flags 100 % of high-band flips in the 32-bit accumulators (G2/G6/G7), incl. all 14 class changes in G2-high; row-sum check C3 flags 65/384 probability flips. Gate (top-2 groups >= 60 % of silent corruptions): PASSED (93 %). Persistent weight-read campaign (384 single-bit flips of one 10-bit weight for a whole window, all 9 layers): logits changed 236, class changed 0. Vote-state campaign (k=5, board clean class stream; 128 history-entry and 128 counter flips): stable decision changed 0 times; 35 history flips changed only the vote count.
entries.limitations: Python INT10 reference with hardware widths; one window per event (no vote state); persistent weight-read and vote-state campaigns not yet run; logical emulation only.
entries.next_action: Protection design focused on the two concentrated points: input-buffer parity (BRAM has spare bits) and a duplicated classifier tail/argmax compare; plus proven-range comparators on accumulators (already 100 % for high-band accumulator flips). Measure silent-corruption reduction on a held-out injection manifest before any B02 build.

entries.hypothesis: Pre-normalisation quality flags plus the integer top-two margin reduce accepted wrong outputs under acquisition faults at >= 90 % clean coverage.
entries.command: python -m tools.export_fpga_testset_raw export --split val --out artifacts/results/fpga_rawinput_valset_20261113; python -m tools.research.q01_quality --out artifacts/research/Q01_20261113
entries.outcome: 2,048 raw windows per split, one non-tachometer channel perturbed per window, bit-exact C-model. Invariance controls hold (gain x2, +25 % offset: accuracy unchanged 97.90 % val). Accuracy under faults (val): clip30 97.75, bits8 97.31, hold 93.12, lag32 96.53 %. Gate on validation (>= 90 % clean coverage, >= 30 % fewer accepted wrong outputs over clip30/bits8/hold/lag32): margin 90.4 % / -78 %; flags 100 % / -73.5 %; flags+margin 90.4 % / -95.5 % (all pass; combined best). Flags catch value faults (hold, bits8 100 %, clip30 80 %) but, as expected, not the circular lag; the margin catches part of every fault. Test (reported once), flags+margin: clean coverage 89 % with 0 accepted wrong (45 without rejection), lag32 5 accepted wrong (74), accepted false-healthy 0 in every condition. First run had a padded lag that created a flat segment (artifact, caught by the run flag); kept in run1_lag_padded_artifact/.
entries.limitations: Modelled digital faults on recorded data (no real ADC); window-level, stateless (rejection lasts exactly while the fault is present); thresholds at clean-validation extremes give ~1 % flags on clean test windows. SUPERSEDED for the calibrated-confidence baseline and the gate assessment by Q01v2 (conf used logits/T instead of s_logits*logits/T; availability cost not reported).
entries.next_action: Q02 (optional): quality counters + margin as research status in hardware; the flags are cheap comparators on the raw words in the ingress.

entries.status: superseded by T01v2 (short events and gate invalid: audit 2026-11-13 finding 1/4)
entries.hypothesis: Finite-horizon integer evidence lowers decision delay versus k-vote at a matched false-switch budget.
entries.outcome: Validation (selection; budget = vote_5 13.87 false switches/10k): vote_5 acc 99.58 %, p95 2; hyst_3 acc 99.68 %, 4.41 fsw/10k, p95 2; evid_64 acc 99.84 %, 11.77 fsw/10k, p95 1. Frozen gate formally passed (p95 -50 %, F1 not lower, unresolved not increased) but the gain is ONE window and hysteresis has 2.7x fewer false switches: no clear dominance. Board test logits (reported once): evid_64 acc 99.71 % / F1 99.47 % / 12.3 fsw/10k vs vote_5 99.08 % / 98.52 % / 18.3; hyst_3 99.22 % / 3.35 fsw/10k / p95 4. 0 dB stream: all policies 16-18 unresolved transitions. Synthetic 2-window events detected: evid 89 %, vote_5 17 %, hyst_3 10 %.
entries.limitations: SUPERSEDED: short events were not guaranteed A->B->A inside recordings, each policy saw different random events, late detections counted as successes, the 4*T cap bounds memory not decision time, and the stream delay used only 4 true changes. Use artifacts/research/T01v2_20261114.
entries.next_action: Hold FPGA implementation (conditional). If pursued: evid_64 needs 4 x ~9-bit counters + margin (top1-top2) in logic.

entries.hypothesis: Bounded background load (CPU, memory, cache, SD, network) does not break the board-side deadline.

An UNBOUNDED 1 Gb/s SSH stream dropped the board Ethernet link (known instability at 1 Gb/s); the link was pinned to 100 Mb/s and the network load bounded to 4 MiB/s.

entries.next_action: Mitigation/wrapper not needed (no misses); report the envelope.

entries.hypothesis: Cheap selective protection (input-buffer parity, duplicated classifier tail, proven-range comparators) removes >= 80 % of silent class corruption.
entries.status: physically-measured (clean behaviour); detection physically measured with logical injection in B03
entries.command: python -m tools.research.fault_injection campaign --seed 20261114 --out artifacts/research/B02_20261113/heldout_campaign; python hls/research/b02_integrity/make_b02_top.py; powershell -File tools/build_raw_core.ps1 -Variant b02
entries.outcome: Protections chosen on the B01 pilot (94.4 % modelled reduction there) and confirmed on a held-out campaign (new seed: new windows and events; injection-off = canonical): silent class corruptions 76 -> 67 (range only), 16 (parity + duplicated tail), 7 (all three) = -90.8 %, above the frozen 80 % gate. Remaining: projection-accumulator mid bits 5, QKV 1, probability 1. Cost under faults: 1,084 flags on faults that did not change the class (availability, not false flags on clean data). Hardware variant B02 v1 (hls/research/b02_integrity/, generated from the canonical raw top): input-buffer XOR signature (write vs after projection read), cls4 + argmax evaluated twice and compared (HLS time-multiplexes both evaluations on ONE compute unit: a repeated computation, not two independent circuits; it does not cover persistent/common-mode faults of the shared unit or weights), projection accumulator range check (bound 719,316 from weights_int10.h); research register integrity_status. Context/FFN range checks left out (0 class changes there in B01). C-model: goldens 41/41 identical + status 0 (incl. edge windows); 95,404 test windows: logits and class identical to canonical, integrity_status 0 on all (0 false flags). Post-route (XC7Z020, 100 MHz): LUT 36,670 -> 37,035 (+1.0 %), FF 36,163 -> 36,606 (+1.2 %), DSP 210 (+0), BRAM 76.5 (+0), WNS +0.202 ns; HLS C-simulation 41/41 exact with integrity_status 0. Overhead gate (<= 5 % LUT, <= 2 DSP, timing) passed. Board (deployment research_b02_z7020_20261113): golden 41/41 incl. 8 ties; full test 95,404/95,404 logits and class = canonical C-model, accuracy 97.7705 %, integrity_status 0 on all 95,404 clean windows (0 false flags); hard real time 0 misses in 30,000, but response p50 17.07 / max 17.71 ms vs 15.96 / 16.63 canonical: +1.1 ms from the range check placed after each projection output in the non-pipelined outer loop (HLS latency 1,613,066 vs 1,502,098 cycles).
entries.limitations: Detection on hardware measured separately in B03 (logical injection overlay, 2026-11-13); latency cost of the range check could be removed by checking in a separate pipelined pass.
entries.next_action: Optional: move the range check off the critical loop to remove the +1.1 ms; a finer projection-accumulator bound (per-output) could catch the mid-bit flips B03 leaves silent.

entries.hypothesis: Path-A combined finalist: unsigned 8-bit attention probabilities (A02 p8u) on top of an exact 8-bit divider keep accuracy within the frozen precision gate and save >= 15 % of one post-route resource versus the canonical core.
entries.command: python hls/research/a06_p8u/make_a06_top.py; g++ exhaustive test hls/research/a06_p8u/test_div_q8_exhaustive.cpp; python -m tools.check_variant_cmodel --research-bits 10,10,8,1 ...; python -m tools.make_variant_golden --research-bits 10,10,8,1 --dst artifacts/research/A06_20261113/golden_raw1024_p8u; python -m tools.run_csim_fulltest --exe tmp/csim/batch_raw_p8u.exe ... --out artifacts/research/A06_20261113/csim_p8u_fulltest; powershell -File tools/build_raw_core.ps1 -Variant a06; python tools/package_seq256_pynq_deploy.py --pkg artifacts/research/A06_20261113/a06_build --bundle artifacts/deploy/research_a06_z7020_20261113 --golden artifacts/research/A06_20261113/golden_raw1024_p8u; python -m tools.raw_core_board_test deploy|golden|fulltest --cmodel artifacts/research/A06_20261113/csim_p8u_fulltest/csim_logits.txt|rt
entries.outcome: Different numerical model with its own reference (research p8u) and own goldens. div_q8 exhaustive: 0 mismatches over 367,657,004 reachable pairs (native and ap_int). C-model = research p8u reference on 600 clean + 600 SNR 0 dB windows; HLS C-simulation 41/41 against its own goldens. Test split (previously explored, selection was on validation): accuracy 97.8848 % vs canonical 97.7705 %, macro-F1 95.857 vs 95.669 (+0.19 pp), recall normal 87.54/87.21, imbalance 97.89/97.78, misalignment 98.93/99.09 (-0.16 pp), bearing 97.88/97.65; class agreement with canonical 94,908/95,404. Precision gate (<= 0.3 pp macro-F1 drop, <= 1 pp recall drop) passed. Post-route (XC7Z020, 100 MHz): LUT 36,670 -> 30,216 (-17.6 %), FF 36,163 -> 28,466 (-21.3 %), DSP 210, BRAM 76.5 unchanged, WNS +0.100 ns, HLS latency 1,502,073 cycles (canonical 1,502,098). Versus A05 (divider only) the 8-bit probabilities add only -2.4 % LUT / -3.2 % FF: almost all of the saving comes from the exact divider. Board (research_a06_z7020_20261113): golden 41/41 incl. 3 ties; full test 95,404/95,404 logits and class register = A06 C-model, accuracy 97.8848 %; hard real time 0 misses in 30,000 (p50 15.98 / max 16.69 ms), 30,200/30,200 outputs = A06 C-model.
entries.limitations: Changes the numerical model (not bit-identical to the canonical deployment: 496 test windows change class); the accuracy difference against canonical is within the bootstrap noise seen on validation; the incremental hardware gain over A05 is small.
entries.next_action: None required. If a smaller core is wanted for the thesis, A05 (bit-identical) is the safer recommendation; A06 shows the probability width is not the bottleneck.

entries.hypothesis: The B02 integrity checks detect class-changing single-bit faults when the faults are injected in the real FPGA datapath (logical injection), with board outputs equal to the bit-exact C-model row by row.
entries.command: python hls/research/b03_inject/make_b03_top.py; powershell -File tools/build_raw_core.ps1 -Variant b03; vivado -mode batch -source hls/f1_int10_seq256/vitis/rerun_impl_strategy.tcl -tclargs tmp/vb03/vb03.xpr Performance_ExplorePostRoutePhysOpt; python tools/package_seq256_pynq_deploy.py --pkg artifacts/research/B03_20261113/b03_build --bundle artifacts/deploy/research_b03_z7020_20261113 --golden hls/f1_int10_seq256/golden_raw1024_argmax; python -m tools.raw_core_board_test deploy|golden; python -m tools.research.b03_campaign manifest|cmodel [--lp64]|board|analyze --out artifacts/research/B03_20261113
entries.outcome: Research overlay = B02 + three programmable injection points (AXI-Lite inj_site/inj_word/inj_bit, written while the core is idle, one ap_start per window): site 1 input-buffer 10-bit word, site 2 projection 32-bit accumulator before the range check, site 3 one logit of classifier tail copy A. Held-out manifest (seed 20261115): 256 test windows (64 per class) x 1 injection-off row + 3 sites x 3 bit bands x 128 events = 1,408 rows. Injection off: C-model full test 95,404/95,404 = canonical with integrity_status 0; board golden 41/41 incl. 8 ties; board injection-off rows 256/256 logits and class = canonical, 0 flags. Board run 1,408 rows in 24.6 s; board = bit-exact C-model on 1,405/1,408 rows and on 1,408/1,408 against a 64-bit-long C-model build: the 3 rows are bit-31 flips of the projection accumulator, where acc + b leaves 32 bits and the Windows (MinGW, 32-bit long) C-model wraps in requant(long) while the synthesized core (64-bit long) does not; all 3 were flagged on both. Physically measured (logical injection): 93 of 1,152 injected faults changed the class; 88 were flagged (94.6 %), 5 silent, all projection-accumulator bits 18-19 (value change 2^18-2^19 stays inside the proven bound 719,316). Site 1: 384/384 flagged by the input signature (30 class changes). Site 3: 384/384 flagged by the repeated tail evaluation (37 class changes; the site-3 flip corrupts one of the two time-multiplexed evaluations). Site 2: 143/384 flagged by the range check (high band 128/128, mid 15/128, low 0/128; low band changed no class). 816 flags on faults that did not change the class (availability cost under faults; 0 flags on clean data). Post-route (XC7Z020, 100 MHz): LUT 37,628 (+2.6 % vs canonical; +1.6 % vs B02 for the injection muxes and registers), FF 37,025 (B02 36,606), DSP 210, BRAM 76.5; default implementation failed timing (WNS -0.437 ns on an existing LayerNorm requant multiply path, kept in b03_build/first_impl_timing_fail/), re-implemented with Performance_ExplorePostRoutePhysOpt: WNS 0.000 ns (met, no margin). HLS latency 1,613,068 cycles (B02 1,613,066).
entries.limitations: Logical injection at three chosen sites only (the sites B01 found vulnerable and B02 protects), one bit per window, transient; not radiation, configuration-memory upsets or timing faults. 128 events per site/band. The research overlay closes timing with zero slack. The Windows desktop C-model differs from the synthesized core only for values outside 32 bits (unreachable in clean operation, proven bound 719,316).
entries.next_action: Thesis/paper: report B03 as physically measured logical-injection coverage with its scope. Optional: per-output projection bounds to catch the bit 18-19 flips.

entries.hypothesis: The exact 9-bit softmax divider is a single expensive operator worth >= 15 % in an isolated HLS/OOC comparison and can replace the generic divider bit-exactly.
entries.command: g++ ... hls/research/a04_softmax_div/test_div_q9_exhaustive.cpp; vitis_hls -f hls/research/a04_softmax_div/run_a04_probe.tcl; vivado -mode batch -source hls/research/a04_softmax_div/ooc_impl.tcl; python -m tools.run_csim_fulltest --exe tmp/csim/batch_raw_divq9.exe ... --out artifacts/research/A04_20261113/csim_divq9_fulltest
entries.outcome: Exhaustive check of div_q9 over all 367,657,004 reachable (numerator, denominator) pairs: 0 mismatches (native and ap_int). Out-of-context operator implementation: -63 % LUT, -74 % FF versus the generic divider. Integrated C-model: 95,404/95,404 test rows identical to the canonical C-model (logits and class). Gate passed; promoted to the integrated build A05.

entries.hypothesis: Bounded-state integer evidence lowers the p95 decision delay by >= 20 % versus the best simple comparator (k-vote, hysteresis) at a matched false-switch budget and maximum horizon (frozen T01 gate).
entries.status: software-measured; gate NOT passed -> FPGA implementation stopped
entries.command: python -m tools.research.temporal_policies_v2 selfcheck --out artifacts/research/T01v2_20261114; python -m tools.research.temporal_policies_v2 run --out artifacts/research/T01v2_20261114
entries.outcome: Immutable manifests (validation seed 20261114: 400 step events + 5 x 300 short events, L = 1,2,4,8,16; segments inside one recording, every label asserted); 12/12 self-checks pass. Validation, matched false-switch budget (vote_5: 13.87 / 10k), H_MAX = 16 windows: best per family vote_5, hyst_3, leaky_0.8, evid_64, evidto_64_6. Step changes (400): p95 delay 2 windows for vote_5 and evid_64 (hyst_3 5, leaky 4), 0 unresolved for all -> p95 reduction 0 % < 20 %: frozen gate NOT passed. Non-gated observations: macro-F1 0.9984 (evid) vs 0.9945 (vote_5); 2-window events detected during the event 262/300 (evid) vs 25/300 (vote_5) and 3/300 (hyst_3); 1-window events 222/300 vs 0; false switches before the step 7 (evid) vs 44 (vote_5) vs 11 (hyst_3); evidto (timeout fallback) behaves like evid on real data and guarantees resolution on zero-margin streams. Test (previously explored, board clean): evid_64 p95 4 vs vote_5 3; L=2 during 266/300 vs 34/300 (+13 only after the event).
entries.limitations: Validation logits from the Python INT10 reference (= canonical numerics); synthetic splices of real windows, not measured fault onsets; the advantage of evidence is in short-event sensitivity and F1, which were not the preregistered criterion.
entries.next_action: Stop the FPGA implementation under the frozen gate. A new, separately preregistered question (short-event detection at a false-switch budget) would be needed to revisit.

entries.hypothesis: Pre-normalisation quality flags plus the integer top-two margin reduce accepted wrong outputs under acquisition faults at >= 90 % clean coverage.
entries.status: software-measured (bit-exact C-model, modelled faults); gate passed for flags, margin, flags+margin
entries.outcome: Same windows/channels as Q01 (seed 20261113). Calibrated confidence with the frozen contract (T=1.42482, s_logits=0.107799): clean validation coverage 0.8999 (just below 90 %), accepted wrong -80.2 % -> gate not passed; superseded formula: threshold had saturated at 0.99999999 (behaved like the margin). Margin: coverage 0.9043, -78.0 %. Flags: coverage 1.0000, -73.5 %, zero accepted under bits8, hold16. Flags+margin: coverage 0.9043, -95.5 %, zero accepted under bits8, hold16. Normal-class clean validation coverage: flags+margin 48.9 %, flags 100 %. White noise 20/10 dB: flags accept 100 %. Bursts (validation, 6 per fault, 20 windows): flags flag bits/hold bursts in the first faulty window and accept the first clean window after; clip50/clip30 caught in 5/6 and 6/6 bursts; lag8/lag32 never flagged. Test (previously explored): flags+margin 0 accepted false-healthy over clean and the 4 gate faults.
entries.limitations: Rejecting every window of a fault is refusing to classify, not better accuracy; the margin threshold costs about half of the clean normal-class windows; modelled digital faults on one channel, not a real acquisition chain.
entries.next_action: Q02 hardware status registers (flags per channel + margin).
